CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess the management of anxiety, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a slight improvement in his overall symptoms. He states that he has been able to achieve better sleep onset, particularly on weekends, where he averages 8-9 hours of sleep. However, he still experiences difficulties falling asleep on work nights, which he attributes to increased anxiety related to upcoming project deadlines. The trazodone at 75 mg continues to help with nocturnal awakenings; however, he still reports early morning awakenings, which he describes as frustrating and fatiguing.
Regarding his persistent fatigue, Mr. Smith notes a modest improvement in energy levels, particularly after initiating dietary changes recommended by the nutritionist. He reports feeling more alert during the day, although he still experiences significant fatigue during high-pressure work periods. He describes his fatigue as a combination of physical exhaustion and mental fatigue, particularly during stressful projects. His headache symptoms have remained stable; he reports experiencing headaches 2-3 times per week with an intensity of 4-6 out of 10. He continues to use ibuprofen 400 mg for relief, approximately 3 times weekly, and expresses concern about the long-term implications of this medication.
Mr. Smith remains committed to his holistic treatment plan, including regular acupuncture sessions, yoga classes, and cognitive-behavioral therapy. He reports that the therapy sessions have been beneficial in developing coping strategies for managing work-related anxiety and stress.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (usage stable) 6. Amitriptyline 40 mg nightly 7. Topiramate 25 mg daily (continue current dosage) 8. Lorazepam 0.5 mg as needed (reduced dosage from 1 mg)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, where he reports that project deadlines remain a significant source of stress. He has been actively engaging in yoga and meditation practices, which he finds helpful for managing stress levels. He abstains from alcohol and maintains a primarily plant-based diet, with an emphasis on whole foods and reduced processed food intake.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Sleep initiation difficulties persist, particularly on work nights; anxiety remains stable with noted improvements; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency remains stable; intensity fluctuates; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/75 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, and appears fatigued but in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with noted fatigue.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Reinforce tapering of lorazepam use to 0.5 mg as needed. Encourage ongoing cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions to further develop coping strategies for work-related stress. 2. Insomnia: Maintain trazodone at 75 mg; continue melatonin at 10 mg; revisit sleep hygiene strategies and consider a sleep study if sleep onset difficulties persist. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue amitriptyline at 40 mg nightly. Given the stable headache frequency and intensity, continue topiramate at 25 mg daily, with plans to reassess in the next visit. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage continued engagement in physical activity and mindfulness practices. Continue working with the nutritionist for dietary optimization and consider discussing alternative therapies if fatigue persists.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2028-11-01 to evaluate ongoing symptoms, assess treatment efficacy, and make further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
